content: Hey all, I've been really wanting to get back into working with simple graphs but I keep avoiding it because I know we're going to do a refactor. I also remember @Bhavik Mehta mentioning that a refactor is unlikely to get a timely review not too long ago - is that still the case?
Is the bottleneck the digraph stuff from here: #graph theory > Digraphs? I get the impression that the digraph PR is what we're prioritizing out of the two
I have very little for mathlib these days, so my current strategy is to wait and see what happens with the digraph refactor before touching simple graphs

Yaël Dillies said:

I have very little for mathlib these days, so my current strategy is to wait and see what happens with the digraph refactor before touching simple graphs

That's what I was thinking too. I'm just starting to get more time now since I'm wrapping up course requirements and want to figure out how I can help move things along...it looks like the PR did get adopted so I don't know if there's anything else I can do for now?

I don't think I've contributed since we switched over to forking for PRs
Please adopt it (mathlib4#33466). It only needs to pass review. I had it passing CI on 27th Feb so it can't have broken too much since then. I haven't had any time to get to it.

One thing you can do is pull my PR into your working branch. Do please add me as co-author in the git commit message (there's a format for that). The file header already has my name in the author list. You could add yours too.
You just need to pull from branch fix_digraph_now of my fork of mathlib4 (Shreyas4991/mathlib4)
